units.text: INT. EARNEST - CONTINUOUS
To please me you are ready to face this fearful ordeal?
units.name: CECILY

units.text: I am!
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: How absurd to talk of the equality of the sexes! Where questions of self-sacrifice are concerned, men are infinitely beyond us.
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: We are.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Clasps hands with Algernon.
They have moments of physical courage of which we women know absolutely nothing.
units.name: CECILY

units.text: To Jack.
Darling!
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: To Cecily.
Darling!
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: They fall into each other’s arms.
Enter Merriman.
When he enters he coughs loudly, seeing the situation.
Ahem! Ahem! Lady Bracknell!
units.name: MERRIMAN

units.text: Good heavens!
units.name: JACK

units.text: Enter Lady Bracknell.
The couples separate in alarm.
Exit Merriman.
Gwendolen! What does this mean?
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Merely that I am engaged to be married to Mr. Worthing, mamma.
units.name: GWENDOLEN

units.text: Come here. Sit down. Sit down immediately. Hesitation of any kind is a sign of mental decay in the young, of physical weakness in the old.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Turns to Jack.

Apprised, sir, of my daughter’s sudden flight by her trusty maid, whose confidence I purchased by means of a small coin, I followed her at once by a luggage train. Her unhappy father is, I am glad to say, under the impression that she is attending a more than usually lengthy lecture by the University Extension Scheme on the Influence of a permanent income on Thought. I do not propose to undeceive him. Indeed I have never undeceived him on any question. I would consider it wrong. But of course, you will clearly understand that all communication between yourself and my daughter must cease immediately from this moment. On this point, as indeed on all points, I am firm.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: I am engaged to be married to Gwendolen, Lady Bracknell!
units.name: JACK

units.text: You are nothing of the kind, sir. And now, as regards Algernon! . . . Algernon!
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Yes, Aunt Augusta.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: May I ask if it is in this house that your invalid friend Mr. Bunbury resides?
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Stammering.
Oh! No! Bunbury doesn’t live here. Bunbury is somewhere else at present. In fact, Bunbury is dead.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Dead! When did Mr. Bunbury die? His death must have been extremely sudden.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Airily.
Oh! I killed Bunbury this afternoon. I mean poor Bunbury died this afternoon.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: What did he die of?
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Bunbury? Oh, he was quite exploded.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: Exploded! Was he the victim of a revolutionary outrage? I was not aware that Mr. Bunbury was interested in social legislation. If so, he is well punished for his morbidity.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: My dear Aunt Augusta, I mean he was found out! The doctors found out that Bunbury could not live, that is what I mean—so Bunbury died.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: He seems to have had great confidence in the opinion of his physicians. I am glad, however, that he made up his mind at the last to some definite course of action, and acted under proper medical advice. And now that we have finally got rid of this Mr. Bunbury, may I ask, Mr. Worthing, who is that young person whose hand my nephew Algernon is now holding in what seems to me a peculiarly unnecessary manner?
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: That lady is Miss Cecily Cardew, my ward.
units.name: JACK

units.text: Lady Bracknell bows coldly to Cecily.
I am engaged to be married to Cecily, Aunt Augusta.
units.name: ALGERNON

units.text: I beg your pardon?
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Mr. Moncrieff and I are engaged to be married, Lady Bracknell.
units.name: CECILY

units.text: With a shiver, crossing to the sofa and sitting down.

I do not know whether there is anything peculiarly exciting in the air of this particular part of Hertfordshire, but the number of engagements that go on seems to me considerably above the proper average that statistics have laid down for our guidance. I think some preliminary inquiry on my part would not be out of place. Mr. Worthing, is Miss Cardew at all connected with any of the larger railway stations in London? I merely desire information. Until yesterday I had no idea that there were any families or persons whose origin was a Terminus.
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL

units.text: Jack looks perfectly furious, but restrains himself.
In a clear, cold voice.
Miss Cardew is the grand-daughter of the late Mr. Thomas Cardew of 149 Belgrave Square, S.W.; Gervase Park, Dorking, Surrey; and the Sporran, Fifeshire, N.B.
units.name: JACK

units.text: That sounds not unsatisfactory. Three addresses always inspire confidence, even in tradesmen. But what proof have I of their authenticity?
units.name: LADY BRACKNELL
